why: The route page puts the start on a ledge just above the Palisade Glacier and mentions snow only on the flat upper part and in the descent gully, so it does not say whether the glacier is crossed.
The route page has the approach going up the North Fork to Third Lake, then over Contact Pass on talus to the north face base, with no glacier travel.
No route page was readable that says whether the snowfield below the buttress is crevassed glacier or a plain snowfield.
Trip reports describe heavy snow on the approach in some years and only small patches in late August, so a normal day is not clear.
A trip report has the party going up the east bowl on rock to a class 4 summit block with no ice or glacier travel.
A trip report describes talus, a loose pass chute and a class 3-4 rock arete to the summit, with no glacier on the line.
The saddle descent is sand or snow depending on the year, and no page read settles which is normal.
One trip report reached the peak across the Middle Palisade Glacier while other lines go by rock from Balcony Peak, so the standard line is not pinned down.
No readable page described the ridge route, and the name alone is not evidence.
No page read describes the saddle descent in the normal season.
No page for this wall was found, so whether the Lilliput Glacier is crossed is unknown.
Pages describe contouring across the toe of the Matterhorn Glacier to a snow couloir, but none says whether crevasses are a hazard.
A ski report crosses the Matterhorn Glacier on rock ribs and firm snow to the couloir, with no mention of crevasses either way.
No page for this route could be found.
The route page says to cross the glacier then climb the couloir, but does not describe crevasses or a bergschrund.
No page read describes the slopes above the pass.
Only search summaries were found, describing a snow and ice couloir and a ridge that is called the Glacier Route by name.

A trip report to this peak by its west ridge stays on rock and cross-country ground with no glacier, and the area has none; the Tombstone Pass line itself was not read. Held at unsure in review: the page read describes a different line.
No page read describes snow on the summer line.
Search summaries say the couloir starts from the glacier below the north face, but no page read describes it.
The route page heads up the glacier to the couloir with rope optional, crampons and axe, and says nothing about crevasses.
